rationale:
All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm), so the decision hinges on study archetype, PRS-comparable performance evidence, and covariate comparability. PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA genetics study (Circulation; Million Veteran Program context) and reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44), which is a PRS-comparable signal and avoids over-interpreting full-model AUROC. The main limitation is that it is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and lacks explicit PRS-only AUC/R2, while several newer genome-wide shrinkage scores exist.

Runners-up: PGS003973 and PGS003972 (same Nat Gen AAA GWAS meta-analysis family; PRS-CS; large multi-cohort development) are strong on disease-focused design but only report full-model discrimination (C-index 0.882 for PGS003973; AUROC 0.69 for PGS003972) with no PRS-only metrics, and covariates are unknown/limitedly specified, reducing comparability. PGS002054 (UKB portability framework) provides a PRS-comparable partial-r (0.0144) but is a framework/portability score rather than disease-focused. PGS001784 (Global Biobank framework) reports a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 of 0.014661 (PRS-comparable) but is also a framework score and its very high full-model AUROC (0.868) is likely largely covariate-driven per the provided domain guidance. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches for the target (alcohol dependence) via trait_efo/phenotyping alignment to alcohol dependence / alcohol use disorder. PGS002738 is best supported because it is explicitly mapped to trait_efo="alcohol dependence" with phenotyping_reported="Alcohol use disorder" and provides the strongest visible discriminative evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51) in a reasonably sized validation (n=7,900) and a disease-focused multi-cohort development context (MVP, UKB). Main limitation: covariates are listed as Unknown and there is no PRS-only AUC/R2, so comparability and standalone PRS contribution cannot be fully assessed from the provided metadata.

Runner-up ordering: PGS002739 remains a strong direct-match (trait_efo="alcohol dependence", AUD phenotype) with supportive OR evidence (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76, 95% CI 1.32–2.34) but is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean ancestry (AFR 100%), making it less generally supported without a specified deployment ancestry. PGS000201 and PGS000202 are direct matches through trait_efo="alcohol dependence measurement" and AUD DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype; however, their visible PRS contribution is weaker (ΔR² 0.01192 and 0.00456, respectively) and they appear to be UKB-only development/validation with no additional robustness signals. Between those siblings, PGS000201 is preferred over PGS000202 due to higher ΔR² and larger validation n (7,599 vs 1,251).

All three candidates are direct matches (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis / near-synonymous trait_reported) so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS004913 is best supported on endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported explicitly matches alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis) and provides PRS-comparable performance evidence (reported R²=0.029 and OR top vs bottom PRS deciles=4.4) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), making its reported signal more interpretable as PRS contribution than models reporting only full-model discrimination. Main limitation: its training/validation sample sizes are modest (n~3k each) and no PRS-only AUROC is provided, so overall strength remains uncertain.

Runners-up: PGS001777 is also endpoint-aligned (alcohol-related cirrhosis) and reports a strong stratification OR (top 20% vs bottom 20% OR=6.18), but it uses only 3 variants, has unknown covariates, and has small validation (n=1,390), reducing confidence in robustness. PGS000704 has very large training/validation and a modern multi-PRS snpnet approach with many variants, but its reported metric is a full-model C-index/AUC=0.711 (not PRS-only) and the publication context is a broad biomarker genetics study rather than clearly disease-focused for alcoholic cirrhosis, so its apparent performance advantage is discounted per the provided domain guidance.

All 19 listed candidates are direct matches to angina pectoris (trait_efo=angina pectoris; phenotyping spans Angina/I20/PheCode 411.3). PGS001262 is best supported because it uses a direct doctor-diagnosed angina endpoint (high endpoint fidelity) and provides both PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.01304) plus incremental AUROC (0.0098) with only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). Its PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.009–0.014; liability h2≈0.134), avoiding obvious metric inflation concerns. Main limitation: the strongest-looking full-model AUROC values in this pool (e.g., 0.807 for PGS001262) are not PRS-comparable and are likely covariate-driven; additionally, the top competitors (PGS001261/PGS001260) come from the same pan-trait UKB sparse-PRS framework family (a known generalization risk per domain guidance), while several newer MVP PheCode models (e.g., PGS005048/PGS005052) report strong per-SD ORs (~1.49) but lack clearly reported PRS-only AUROC/R2 and have N/A training sample details in the visible metadata—so the overall choice remains somewhat uncertain, yielding a sub-optimal (not high-confidence) direct-match selection.

All 9 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo=ankylosing spondylitis; phenotyping_reported is ankylosing spondylitis or a closely related TTE formulation), so a direct-match selection is possible. PGS002089 is preferred because it is a genome-wide shrinkage-style model (LDpred2) with a large variant set (22,026) and reports a stronger PRS-comparable metric than the other portability-family option (partial correlation 0.0919 vs 0.0797 for PGS001876), while maintaining the same endpoint and broadly similar UKB-based covariate adjustment. Main limitation: the strongest-looking AUCs are from different study families and are not PRS-only comparable (the EAS-focused models report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates; the snpnet pan-trait UKB models are explicitly a framework family that domain guidance warns often generalizes poorly), and PGS002089 itself lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 in the visible metadata—so the choice is supported structurally but remains uncertain, lowering confidence to Moderate. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates for aortic stenosis are present (PGS005252, PGS005254) plus closely aligned aortic valve function measures mapped to aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256). PGS005252 is best supported because it is an exact trait match (trait_reported/trait_efo = aortic stenosis) with endpoint-fidelity phenotyping (incident aortic stenosis cases), a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDPred2) with large variant count (~1.12M), and it reports a strong time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) alongside a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.92). The main limitation is that the reported discrimination is a full-model metric with many clinical covariates (e.g., T2D, HTN, CAD, hyperlipidemia, BMI, smoking, renal failure), so it may be substantially covariate-driven and not directly comparable to PRS-only performance; no PRS-only AUROC/R² is provided, lowering certainty. Runners-up: PGS005254 is also an exact aortic stenosis model with incident endpoint and clean/basic covariates, but has less visible performance detail (HR 1.64 only; no AUC/C-index). PGS005255 and PGS005256 are aortic stenosis–mapped valve-function traits from the same publication family with similar endpoint/covariates and moderate HR (~1.53), but are less direct than an explicit aortic stenosis PRS. Among remaining non-matching models, PGS004911 (hypertrophic cardiomyopathy MTAG) is included only as a distant fallback from the visible list; it is not phenotype-aligned to aortic stenosis, so it provides weak direct-match support.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (arthritis) are present, including exact EFO matches (PGS001135: “Arthritis (nos)” with trait_efo=arthritis; PGS004477/PGS004547: “M13 (Other arthritis)” with trait_efo=arthritis). PGS001135 is the best-supported direct match because it is explicitly arthritis (nos) with reported PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.53928; PGS-only R2=0.00291) and a full-model AUROC (0.67424) plus incremental AUROC (0.00314), enabling interpretation of PRS contribution (and consistent with the provided arthritis heritability ceiling guidance). However, overall evidence remains sub-optimal because the PRS-only signal is small and the model comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework (“Significant sparse polygenic risk scores across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused scores in external validation. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS004547 and PGS004477 are exact arthritis EFO matches but provide only a single OR without PRS-only metrics and appear to be risk-factor/disease-PRS integration framework outputs; PGS000114 (juvenile idiopathic arthritis) is arthritis-spectrum and disease-focused with stronger reported discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.738) but is a pediatric subtype mismatch for generic ‘arthritis’; PGS004873 (incident rheumatoid arthritis) is arthritis-spectrum with strong full-model C-index (0.85) but is not the generic arthritis endpoint and is time-to-event/incident-focused.

All listed candidates are direct matches to asthma (trait_efo=asthma), so selection hinges on endpoint fidelity plus PRS-comparable performance evidence and study archetype. PGS002061 (LDpred2; UKB-derived) is preferred because it is a direct asthma endpoint (phenotyping_reported: Asthma), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with large variant count (793,375), and reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.1184 with CI) rather than relying on covariate-inflated full-model AUROC. Key limitation: the context does not provide PRS-only AUROC/R² for most candidates, making cross-model performance comparisons uncertain; several alternatives have strong-looking full-model AUROC but are either from pan-trait/framework families (e.g., snpnet ‘813 traits’) or have potentially non-comparable covariate packaging (e.g., family/environment risk scores), so confidence is not high. Runners-up: PGS001344 has strong reported discrimination (full_model AUROC 0.666 with PGS-only AUROC/R² also provided) but comes from a pan-trait UKB framework paper, which domain guidance penalizes versus disease-focused scores; PGS001782 and PGS001787 are genome-wide PRS-CS-auto scores from a global biobank framework with moderate full-model AUROC and covariates-regressed-out R², but framework context and metric comparability remain limitations; PGS001849 is another UKB portability-framework asthma score with similar PRS-comparable partial-r evidence (0.1135) but slightly weaker than PGS002061. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct EFO matches to atopic eczema, but several have endpoint mismatches (paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis) or non-PRS-comparable performance reporting (full-model AUROC only, or coefficients/p-values without standard PRS discrimination metrics). PGS002755 is the best-supported direct-match because its phenotyping_reported is incident atopic dermatitis (aligned to the target), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; 1,090,702 variants), and it reports a PRS effect size (HR 1.249, 95% CI 1.123–1.391) in a large European evaluation (n=337,910), providing at least some PRS-comparable evidence without relying on a therapy-specific endpoint. Main limitation: none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only AUROC/R²; PGS002755’s HR is modest (<1.5) and comparability across studies is limited, so the overall direct-match recommendation remains sub-optimal rather than high-confidence.

All listed candidates are direct matches to atrial fibrillation (or AF/flutter) by trait_reported/trait_efo and generally coherent phenotyping_reported, so this is a direct-match selection problem. PGS005168 is best supported in the visible evidence because it comes from a disease-focused, large AF meta-analysis publication (Nat Genet; >180,000 cases per title), reports strong discrimination (C-index 0.8718 with CI) and a strong per-SD effect size (HR 1.6663), and uses a largely demographic/standard clinical risk adjustment set (age, age^2, sex, array) plus CHARGE-AF (a named clinical risk calculator), which is a comparability concern but does not fully negate the unusually strong and disease-focused evidence package. Main limitation: inclusion of CHARGE-AF in covariates suggests some risk-wrapper packaging, so the reported C-index may be partly covariate-driven and is not a pure PRS-only metric; several other candidates have cleaner covariate sets but weaker/less complete performance evidence.

Runners-up rationale (ranked): PGS002814 is also disease-focused with extremely large training GWAS (n=1,150,799) and strong reported OR (~1.94) with AUROC 0.74 in East Asian evaluation, but it is EAS-evaluated (not EUR) and uses P+T with fewer variants. PGS005313 is a recent cross-population AF study with strong OR (1.82) and AUROC 0.78, but evaluation is MAE-only and the single-record evidence is thinner than PGS005168. PGS000016 (Khera et al., Nat Genet 2019) is a classic LDpred genome-wide score with explicit PRS-only R2 (0.029) and basic covariates, but its reported AUROC is full-model and the PRS-only signal appears modest. PGS000331 (Nat Med 2020) is disease-focused with multi-cohort development and HR 1.62 plus C-index 0.751, but overall performance evidence is less compelling than the top choices. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 4 candidates are direct matches to the target trait concept (atrial flutter appears in trait_reported/trait_efo for each; two are flutter-only vs three are AF+flutter composites). PGS001263 is preferred because it is the only flutter-specific endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Atrial flutter”) and it reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.61716; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.02517) with basic covariates; its PRS-only R2 is also below the provided local heritability ceiling (h2_obs=0.0157; h2_liability=0.1443), so nothing is obviously inconsistent. Main limitation: PGS001263 (and PGS001339) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as tending to generalize poorly; meanwhile the portability-study models (PGS002050/PGS001841) use genome-wide shrinkage/penalized regression and larger training n but lack PRS-only AUROC/R2, making direct performance comparison uncertain. Runners-up ranking: PGS001339 is next-best on visible evidence (still reports PRS-only metrics but is a broader AF+flutter time-to-event endpoint); among the two portability-study AF+flutter models, PGS002050 is slightly preferred over PGS001841 due to marginally higher partial-r (0.1034 vs 0.1026) with otherwise similar endpoint/covariates/ancestry context.

Two direct-match candidates are visible (PGS000327, PGS002790), both mapped to autism spectrum disorder (trait_reported/trait_efo). PGS000327 is best supported because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly aligned to the target endpoint (“Autism spectrum disorder”), and it comes from a disease-focused ASD GWAS publication context (“Identification of common genetic risk variants for autism spectrum disorder.”). It also provides supportive PRS signal evidence via an OR=1.33 (moderate per domain guidance) and a higher reported full_model_r2 (0.0245) than the alternative, with basic covariates (genetic PCs, genotyping wave) and EUR evaluation.

PGS002790 is a weaker direct match despite the same trait_reported/trait_efo because its phenotyping_reported is explicitly different (“Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)”), suggesting endpoint-fidelity mismatch/metadata incoherence relative to ASD diagnosis; its reported metric is a smaller partial R² (~0.00546) and it lacks effect size reporting. Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL (not high-quality) because neither model reports clearly PRS-only discrimination metrics (e.g., PGS-only AUC/R²), and the best model’s performance evidence is limited to a modest OR and a full-model R², which are less directly comparable for PRS ranking.

All 20 visible candidates are direct matches on concept (trait_efo = basal cell carcinoma). The strongest support comes from the coherent Cancer PRSweb (Am J Hum Genet, 2020-12-15) cluster with identical endpoint wording (phenotyping_reported = Basal cell carcinoma), basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), EUR development/evaluation, and comparable reported metrics. Within that cluster, PGS000452 is best supported because it has the highest reported full-model AUROC (0.632, tied) and the strongest accompanying effect-size evidence (OR per SD 1.663) plus the largest reported Nagelkerke R² (0.0487) among the tied-AUROC siblings, indicating the most consistent discrimination signal in the visible metadata. Runners-up are the closest near-clones with essentially identical endpoint/covariates and nearly identical AUROC/R²/effect sizes: PGS000454 (AUROC 0.632, OR 1.661, R² 0.0489), PGS000456 (AUROC 0.630, OR 1.633, R² 0.0456), and PGS000458 (AUROC 0.628, OR 1.634, R² 0.0457). PGS000730 is next-best outside that family due to large evaluation size (n=88,924) and strong OR (1.57), but has unknown covariates and lacks supporting R²/CI detail, lowering comparability. Confidence is Moderate because none of the candidates report PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R², so the full-model AUROC/R² may be partially covariate-driven and small differences among the top PRSweb siblings may not be meaningful. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (all map to the target EFO concept bilirubin metabolism disease). PGS001824 is preferred because its endpoint is the most phenotype-aligned and specific to the target (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion” with trait_efo exactly “bilirubin metabolism disease”), and it reports a PRS-comparable metric (partial correlation 0.0716 in European validation). PGS002032 is a near-clone direct match with the same endpoint and identical partial-r, but with a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) and far higher variant count; however, the visible evidence does not provide any performance separation between the two siblings, so the choice remains uncertain. PGS000924 is also a direct match but is a time-to-event composite endpoint (“porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism”) from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework (813 traits) with an unusually high reported R2/AUROC relative to the provided heritability sanity-check context, making its apparent performance advantage less reliable for selection. Overall, direct matches exist but the best pick is limited by missing standard PRS-only AUC/R2 for the two most phenotype-faithful candidates and by near-indistinguishability between them. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All three visible candidates are direct lexical/EFO matches to the target bipolar disorder spectrum (bipolar disorder; bipolar I; bipolar II) and share the same publication, method (SDPR), EUR-only GWAS/EVAL ancestry, similar variant counts (~935k–949k), and similar basic covariates (age, PCs1-3), so none has a clearly superior evidence package. None reports PRS-comparable AUC or PRS-only R²; only small partial R² values are shown and the phenotyping_reported fields appear non-diagnostic (cognition/behavior measures rather than bipolar diagnosis), creating endpoint-fidelity ambiguity that prevents a high-quality direct-match recommendation. PGS002786 is selected narrowly because it matches the umbrella target label exactly (bipolar disorder) and has the largest variant count among the otherwise near-clone set; runners-up are the subtype-specific siblings, with ordering weakly supported by their similar partial R² values.

All three visible candidates are direct matches at the EFO level to the target umbrella concept (“blood coagulation disease”), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence quality. PGS001033 is the only model explicitly mapped to the target EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) and it provides the richest directly comparable performance evidence (includes PGS-only AUROC 0.634 and PGS-only R² 0.0578, plus a European validation AUROC with CI), with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). The main limitation is that its phenotyping is time-to-event (“TTE other coagulation defects”) and it comes from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as a generalizability risk; additionally, it is extremely sparse (1 variant), which is structurally weak for a broad disease umbrella.

For runners-up, PGS002034 and PGS001826 target a narrower but clearly within-scope congenital clotting-factor deficiency endpoint (phenotyping matches their trait_reported), and both come from the same UKB portability framework paper; however, they lack AUROC/R² and only report partial-r (~0.056), limiting comparability. Between them, PGS002034 is structurally preferred over PGS001826 because it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with many variants (32,552) versus penalized regression with 45 variants, while their reported partial-r is essentially identical. Overall, because the best candidate is framework-derived and endpoint/time-to-event vs congenital-subtype differences remain unresolved with limited comparable metrics for two models, the direct-match set supports only a sub-optimal recommendation.

Direct-match candidates are abundant for the target trait (breast carcinoma / breast cancer). Among the visible candidates, PGS004153 is best supported as a direct-match because it has (i) exact trait alignment (trait_efo=breast carcinoma; phenotyping_reported=Breast cancer), (ii) a method with explicit multi-score aggregation (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV), which domain knowledge flags as a strong structural advantage over single-score constructions, and (iii) strong reported discrimination within its evaluation set (full_model AUROC ~0.6625 with accompanying R² ~0.0764 and OR ~1.83). The main limitation is that these are not explicitly PRS-only metrics (covariates listed as 0, but the catalog field is still ‘full_model’), so cross-model comparability is imperfect and confidence is reduced. Runners-up are other high-performing, endpoint-aligned models from the same five-biobank evaluation family with very similar phenotype/covariate framing but slightly weaker reported AUROC/R²/OR: LDpred2.CV (PGS004040), LDpred2-auto (PGS004025), PRS-CS-auto (PGS004083), and megaprs.CV (PGS004069).

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to celiac disease via trait_efo="celiac disease" and largely aligned phenotyping_reported. PGS000316 is best supported because it targets the generic clinical endpoint (phenotyping_reported="Coeliac disease"), is disease-focused (pilot clinical care diagnosis aid study rather than a pan-trait/portability framework), and reports strong discrimination (full-model AUROC=0.879 with CI 0.87–0.888) in a very large European validation (n=379,767). Main limitation: the reported AUROC is a full-model metric with covariates listed as Unknown, so PRS-only performance cannot be isolated from the visible metadata.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001301 has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.82867; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.14224) and aligned phenotype ("Malabsorption/coeliac disease"), but comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (813 traits), which domain guidance penalizes versus disease-focused models when direct disease-focused options exist. (2) PGS000040 is disease-focused and reports very high AUROC=0.9, but this is also a full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and smaller validation (n=2,476), making it less robust/comparable. (3–4) PGS000042 and PGS000041 are restricted to HLA-DQ2.5 carriers (endpoint narrower than generic celiac disease) and have lower full-model AUROC (~0.73/0.718), so they are weaker direct matches for the general target despite being disease-focused. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_efo=cervical carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported consistently cervical cancer, mostly incident cervical cancer). Best-supported is PGS003428 because it comes from a cervical-phenotype-focused GWAS meta-analysis paper and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred) with very large variant coverage (2,894,555), which is structurally favored for polygenic traits when endpoint alignment is acceptable; it also reports a moderate per-SD HR (1.33). However, confidence is limited because it lacks PRS-only metrics (only a full-model C-index=0.613) and its reported discrimination is not directly comparable across candidates with different covariate sets. Runners-up: PGS000073 and PGS000784 have strong endpoint fidelity (incident cervical cancer) and large EUR evaluation (n=211,795) with similar reported full-model AUROC (~0.745) and HR (~1.21–1.22), but they are GWAS-hits style (10 variants) and the AUROC is full-model with multiple epidemiologic covariates, so PRS-only strength is unclear; PGS005165 is a direct cervical cancer score in an East Asian context (EAS GWAS/EVAL) with HR~1.2 but is also GWAS-hits (15 variants) and has only full-model C-index=0.566; PGS003389 (lassosum, 2,814 variants) has weaker reported full-model AUROC (0.563) and minimal R² (0.00158). PGS001299 is deprioritized despite having explicit PGS-only metrics because it is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (snpnet, 24 variants) with weak PRS-only AUROC (~0.55) and very small PGS R² (~0.0026), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused models.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to cholelithiasis by trait fields, but the evidence is mixed and often lacks PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R²), lowering certainty. PGS004546 is selected as best because it is an exact ICD10 K80 cholelithiasis endpoint (phenotyping_reported), evaluated in EUR, and—within its same-publication sibling pair (Commun Biol 2024, same cohorts/variant count/endpoint)—it reports the stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.2986 vs 1.2194 for PGS004476), which is the main available differentiator given missing AUC/R². Runners-up: PGS004476 is the closest sibling with the same endpoint but weaker OR. PGS005150 is an exact cholelithiasis endpoint with a modern cross-ancestry PRS-CSx construction (BBJ+UKB GWAS; EAS evaluation), but it reports only a beta (not directly comparable to OR/HR here) and is evaluated only in EAS, making it less generally supported from the visible evidence. PGS002072 and PGS001861 are direct but use a broader composite endpoint (cholelithiasis and cholecystitis) and come from a UKB portability framework paper; they provide partial-r metrics but no PRS-only AUROC/R², and framework context is a negative signal versus disease-focused endpoint-faithful models. PGS001174, despite having explicit PGS-only AUROC/R² and incremental AUROC, is deprioritized because it is a pan-trait sparse UKB framework score with a time-to-event phenotype, which domain guidance flags as often underperforming disease-focused alternatives when such alternatives exist.

All listed candidates are direct matches to the target trait (CKD) via trait_efo and generally CKD-relevant phenotyping. PGS002237 is best supported because it is explicitly CKD-focused with a clear clinical threshold endpoint (CKD stage 3+ / eGFR<45), large development sample (n=279,819), multi-ancestry evaluation, and reports strong discrimination evidence in its selected validation record (AUROC 0.78) plus a moderate per-SD effect size (OR 1.47). Key limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric with substantial clinical covariates (hypertension, diabetes, BMI, medication use, etc.), and no PGS-only AUROC/R² is provided, so PRS-only performance comparability is uncertain.

Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005090 has very strong reported metrics (AUROC 0.9; R² 0.1; OR 1.41) but is AFR-only GWAS/EVAL and thus less generally supported without a specified deployment ancestry; PGS005113 has a strong OR (1.35) and CKDGen training but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS004889 is incident CKD (without diabetes) with multi-ancestry evaluation and HR 1.3 but includes a bundled clinical risk score covariate, reducing PRS comparability; PGS002757 is a clean CKD label with modest OR (1.15) and limited performance detail. Several 2023 AJHG ‘five biobanks’ CKD-or-dialysis models show similar full-model AUROCs (~0.58–0.59) with covariates=0, but their discrimination is materially weaker than the above and they form a near-tied cluster, so they are not prioritized as top runners-up.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo = chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). PGS001788 is preferred because it is an exact COPD endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both COPD) and comes from a large multi-biobank development context (Cell Genom “Global Biobank analyses…”, PRS-CS-auto, genome-wide variant count ~910k), which domain guidance treats as methodologically stronger than sparse UKB-only framework scores and more likely to generalize. However, the evidence is limited by lack of clearly PRS-only AUROC and reliance on a single-record summary; the reported AUROC (0.715) appears as a generic classification metric and is not explicitly PGS-only, so it cannot be cleanly compared across candidates. As runners-up: PGS001783 is the closest sibling from the same study family with higher reported covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.038092 vs 0.0163) and slightly higher AUROC (0.74) but much smaller validation n (7,128), making the tradeoff ambiguous. Among the UKB snpnet COPD-labeled models, PGS001332/PGS001333/PGS001334 have coherent endpoint alignment and explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2, but they are from the “813 traits” sparse pan-trait UKB framework that domain guidance flags as typically less externally robust; within that cluster, PGS001334 has the strongest PGS-only metrics but is time-to-event, while PGS001332 is the most straightforward COPD label. Overall, one best choice is identifiable but meaningful competition and metric comparability limitations keep confidence below high. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 6 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (cirrhosis of liver) via either exact EFO mapping (cirrhosis of liver) or a closely aligned subtype (alcoholic/alcohol-associated cirrhosis). PGS004621 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint alignment (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported both ‘Cirrhosis’), a modern genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with very large genome-wide variant coverage (1,089,806 variants), and disease-focused multi-cohort development/validation context (multiple biobanks listed; validation_sample_size n=1,153,995) with reported discrimination (AUROC 0.68) and an effect size (OR 1.42). Main limitation: none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only (covariate-free) AUROC/R²; the AUROC values shown are full-model style metrics, so cross-model comparability is limited and confidence cannot be high.

Runners-up: PGS000726 is an exact cirrhosis EFO match with moderate per-SD OR (1.32) and an additional stratified OR (top 20% vs bottom 20% = 2.26) from a disease-focused cirrhosis GWAS study, but it is a sparse 12-variant GWS score and lacks AUROC/R². PGS004908 is best supported in the visible evidence because it has strong endpoint alignment (phenotyping_reported: Kidney cancer), reports the strongest discrimination among candidates with comparable reported metrics (AUROC 0.74, EUR eval) and the strongest per-SD effect size signal (OR 1.5, 95% CI 1.43–1.58), with covariates that are standard epidemiologic adjustments (age, sex, PCs, BMI, smoking, hypertension) rather than obvious risk-wrapper packaging. Key limitation: the AUROC shown is a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2), so comparability across studies is imperfect and confidence is moderated. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS000076 and PGS000787 are highly endpoint-faithful (incident kidney cancer) with similar full-model AUROC (~0.722) and HR (~1.15–1.16) in large EUR evaluations; PGS000722 has weaker AUROC (0.567) but strong endpoint alignment and large validation; PGS004690 uses a genome-wide method (AnnoPred; 6.35M variants) but has modest AUROC (0.5644) and unknown covariates, limiting interpretability.

Direct-match candidates for the target trait (kidney failure) are present, including PGS000708 (trait_reported/trait_efo: Kidney failure) and two N18 chronic renal failure models (PGS004492, PGS004562; trait_efo: kidney failure). PGS000708 is best supported on endpoint fidelity because its phenotyping_reported explicitly targets kidney failure ("Diabetic kidney failure in all") and it reports a time-to-event effect size (HR 1.19, 95% CI 1.13–1.26) plus a full-model C-index of 0.779 with only basic covariates (age as time scale, sex, batch, PCs), which is comparatively clean. However, the evidence is still sub-optimal because the reported discrimination is full-model (not PGS-only), and the phenotype is restricted to a diabetic kidney failure subtype rather than generic kidney failure. Runners-up: PGS004562 and PGS004492 are also direct kidney-failure EFO matches (N18 chronic renal failure) with moderate-to-strong per-SD ORs (1.395 and 1.171 respectively) but have unknown covariates and no AUC/R2, limiting comparability; PGS002237 is a strong disease-focused CKD stage 3+ model (AUROC 0.78; OR 1.47) but is not kidney-failure-specific; PGS004158 is the best-performing among the coherent CKD-or-dialysis sibling cluster (AUROC ~0.592; OR ~1.389; covariates=0) but remains CKD/dialysis rather than kidney failure specifically.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (knee osteoarthritis / gonarthrosis of knee) via trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but the pool has limited PRS-comparable performance reporting (most lack PGS-only AUROC/R²), so the best choice is not unequivocal.

Best pick (PGS002767): Direct endpoint match (phenotyping_reported: “Knee osteoarthritis”; trait_efo: osteoarthritis, knee) with genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS; 1,052,275 variants) and a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.35, 95% CI 1.3–1.4) in a reasonably sized EUR evaluation (n=39,444) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical). This provides the clearest PRS-specific signal among candidates that are not pan-trait framework scores.

Why not others as best: PGS002729 is also a clean direct match and disease-focused, but its only visible discrimination is a full-model AUROC (0.66) with BMI included and no PGS-only metrics, making PRS contribution less directly comparable. PGS004549/PGS004479 are direct-match UKB-derived models but come from a risk-factor integration paper with unknown covariates and only OR point estimates (no CI/AUC), limiting interpretability. PGS004883 reports a C-index (0.60) and HR=1.37 but appears to have very small training (n=404) and is incident/time-to-event packaged, reducing confidence. PGS001192 reports explicit PGS-only metrics but is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”), which domain guidance flags as typically underperforming disease-focused alternatives despite well-formatted metrics.

Main limitation driving DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL: absence of consistent PRS-only AUROC/R² across the leading disease-focused candidates (and heterogeneous endpoint framing such as incident/TTE and knee replacement) prevents a high-confidence single winner based solely on the visible evidence.

All 5 candidates are direct matches at the concept level (trait_reported/trait_efo indicate late-onset Alzheimer’s disease), so a direct-match exists. Among them, PGS000054 and PGS000053 form a coherent, disease-focused sibling pair (same publication, same method: genome-wide significant variants, same variant count=21, same phenotyping_reported: familial late-onset Alzheimer’s disease, and basic covariates age/sex). Between these near-clones, PGS000054 has the stronger reported PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.73 vs 1.29 for PGS000053), which is the most comparable performance evidence available here (no PRS-only AUC/R² is provided for any model). Main limitation: the strongest candidate is evaluated in AMR (Hispanic/Latin American) rather than EUR, while most other candidates are EUR-evaluated; additionally, several other models have missing/less comparable performance reporting (e.g., PGS000334 reports an R²=0.191 from C+T with unknown covariates, which is difficult to interpret as PRS-only and may be inflated; PGS004918 reports only a full-model AUROC=0.731 with unknown covariates and small validation n=136; PGS002289’s phenotyping_reported appears cognition/age-interaction rather than a clean AD diagnosis endpoint despite the trait label), so overall evidence is not clean enough for a high-confidence pick.

Direct-match candidates for lung cancer are present (multiple models with trait_reported/phenotyping_reported explicitly lung cancer or lung/bronchus cancer). PGS000078 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint alignment (incident lung cancer), large European evaluation (n=392,539), and includes effect-size evidence (HR=1.16, 95% CI 1.11–1.22) alongside high reported discrimination in its selected validation record (AUROC=0.846; C-index=0.849). Key limitation: the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with extensive covariates (including family history, PM2.5, and detailed smoking terms/interactions), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, so the PRS-specific contribution cannot be isolated; this keeps confidence below High. Runners-up: PGS000789 is essentially the same 109-variant lung cancer score evaluated in the same large incident-lung-cancer setting with similar metrics (AUROC=0.846; HR=1.17) but uses inverse weights, making it hard to justify over the original without additional evidence. PGS004860 reports very high AUROC (0.893) but is a case-control French-Canadian cohort with no PRS-only metrics and still includes covariates, so comparability/transportability is less clear. PGS000740 has strong study support and good AUROC (0.811) but targets early-onset lung cancer (<50), which is a restricted endpoint relative to generic lung cancer. PGS000721 is a direct lung cancer model with moderate AUROC (0.738) and similar covariates to several smaller-validation models, but has much smaller validation (n=1,202) and lacks PRS-only metrics. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present (12 models) and all are concept-aligned to lupus erythematosus (either EFO lupus erythematosus or systemic lupus erythematosus). Best-supported overall is PGS002082 because it is an exact EFO match to the target (lupus erythematosus), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (361,553), and is evaluated across multiple ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS), which is supportive for transportability; it also reports a (modest) PRS-comparable metric (partial-r 0.0212). Key limitation: no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is reported for any candidate here, and several alternatives report higher full-model AUROC but those are not PRS-comparable; additionally, some candidates have endpoint restrictions or covariate/packaging concerns (e.g., PGS003960 includes a phenotype risk score covariate, suggesting leakage). Runners-up: PGS001870 is the same portability study with exact EFO match but weaker method/metric (penalized regression, fewer variants, lower partial-r). Among disease-focused SLE models, PGS000328 has strong reported full-model AUROC (0.83) on a large validation (n=1,001) but is restricted to early-onset SLE; PGS000754 is genome-wide (lassosum; 293,684 variants) with broad SLE endpoint but lower full-model AUROC (0.65); PGS000196 is SLE diagnosis in an arthritis outpatient context (potentially narrower clinical setting) with full-model AUROC 0.79 but small validation (n=245). Overall evidence is sufficient for a preferred direct match but remains limited/incomparable across candidates, so the direct-match outcome is sub-optimal rather than high-quality.

Direct-match candidates are present (multiple models mapped to lymphoid leukemia / lymphocytic leukemia). PGS000077 is the best-supported direct match because its phenotyping_reported is an incident lymphocytic leukemia endpoint aligned to the target, it uses a reasonably sized GW-significant variant set (75 SNPs), and it has large European evaluation (n=391,338) with supportive effect size evidence (HR=1.45) under basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs). However, the evidence is not unequivocally high-quality for standalone PRS ranking because the reported discrimination is full-model (AUROC/C-index) rather than explicitly PGS-only, and a close competitor exists: PGS000788 uses the same 75-variant backbone and shows stronger reported full-model metrics and HR (HR=1.7), but its method description (inverse variant weights) introduces uncertainty about PRS construction fidelity relative to the original. Other runners-up are direct but have weaker or less comparable evidence: PGS000645 and PGS002305 are lymphoid leukemia matches but show modest AUROC (~0.58 and ~0.57) with small validation sizes; PGS003453 is a coherent CLL endpoint with strong OR but is subtype-specific (chronic lymphocytic leukemia) rather than the broader lymphoid leukemia target. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 7 candidates are direct matches to the target concept (macular degeneration / age-related macular degeneration), but they vary in endpoint fidelity and in whether reported metrics are PRS-comparable. PGS004606 is best supported overall because it has clean phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD GWAS/meta-analysis context (Nat Genet 2024; IAMDGC), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS; ~1.0M variants), and provides supportive performance/effect evidence (full-model AUROC 0.71 and OR 1.76 per SD in the selected record). Runners-up: PGS004952 reports a very high AUROC but it appears to be a full-model metric (and the AUROC value is inconsistently formatted as 84.2), with a much smaller validation sample (n=1,232) and a narrower endpoint (late AMD), so it is strong but less reliable/comparable; PGS004607 is a sibling PRS-CS score from the same Nat Genet study but with weaker reported discrimination/effect (AUROC 0.65; OR 1.48) and GWAS ancestry AFR with EUR evaluation; PGS001013 is an exact-label macular degeneration model but is from a pan-trait UKB sparse framework (snpnet; 53 variants) with low PGS-only AUROC (~0.553) and small incremental AUROC, which domain guidance flags as typically weaker than disease-focused scores; among the UKB portability-framework options, PGS002041 (LDpred2; genome-wide) has slightly stronger partial-r than PGS001834 and is structurally stronger than the sparse/handpicked-variant PGS002269 whose phenotyping_reported is a retinal thickness biomarker proxy rather than direct AMD diagnosis. Main limitation: across the top candidates, the most comparable PRS-only metrics are largely missing (most report only full-model AUROC or effect sizes), so confidence is reduced and the ranking relies heavily on endpoint fidelity + study archetype + method/variant structure.

Direct-match melanoma PRS candidates are present (multiple models with trait_efo=melanoma and melanoma/cutaneous melanoma phenotyping). PGS000813 is best supported in the visible list because it has strong endpoint alignment (familial cutaneous melanoma in non-carriers of CDKN2A mutation; still melanoma diagnosis), and it reports the strongest PRS-associated effect size evidence among the melanoma-labeled candidates shown (OR per SD 2.12, plus strong stratification OR top 10% vs middle 20% 5.7) along with a high reported AUROC (0.77) in European evaluation. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support combining endpoint fidelity and reported discrimination: PGS000743 (melanoma; full-model AUROC 0.74 but with extensive traditional risk-factor covariates, making the AUROC less PRS-comparable), then PGS002247 and PGS002246 (incident invasive melanoma; moderate-high AUROC ~0.69 with R² ~0.07 in EUR), then PGS000744 (melanoma; strong OR per SD 1.66 but no AUROC reported). Main limitation: many candidates report only full-model AUROC (often with differing covariate sets) and several are from different study archetypes/endpoints (incident vs familial vs dx/hx), so cross-model metric comparability is imperfect, lowering confidence from High to Moderate.

All 6 candidates are nominal direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (multiple myeloma / plasma cell myeloma), but one (PGS003450) has an explicit endpoint mismatch in phenotyping_reported ("Chronic lymphocytic leukemia"), making it weaker for direct-match despite sharing the myeloma label elsewhere. Among the remaining coherent myeloma-endpoint models, PGS002281 is best supported by (i) phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Multiple myeloma), (ii) comparatively strong reported discrimination in the visible record (full_model AUROC 0.644 with CI) and a strong risk gradient (OR 3.18 highest vs lowest quintiles), and (iii) basic demographic covariates (age/sex/region) without obvious heavy clinical leakage. Confidence is not High because none of the candidates report clearly PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 are null across the set), so the AUROC values are full-model and not strictly comparable across differing covariate sets; additionally, PGS002306 shows an even higher full-model AUROC (0.69) but on a much smaller validation sample (n=290) with unknown covariates, creating meaningful competition and uncertainty. Runners-up are ranked by remaining endpoint fidelity plus strength/clarity of the visible performance/effect-size evidence and covariate transparency: PGS002306 next (highest AUROC but limited/unclear evaluation context), then the PRSweb cluster (PGS000653/PGS000654/PGS000652) with consistent myeloma phenotyping and basic covariates but lower full-model AUROC (~0.576–0.577) and modest per-SD ORs (~1.32; PGS000652 weaker).

All 7 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (multiple sclerosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, so a direct-match exists. PGS002726 is best supported because it is disease-focused (IMSGC training cohort; Brain paper explicitly about MS susceptibility) and reports strong discrimination evidence in its selected European validation record (full-model AUROC=0.80 with an additional large effect-size-style metric: OR top 10% vs median=15.0). However, confidence is limited because its covariates are listed as 'Unknown' and it does not report PRS-only AUROC/R², so the AUROC may not be directly comparable across models per the provided domain guidance. Runners-up: PGS000809 is also disease-focused with multi-cohort GWAS context and reports full-model AUROC=0.765 and R²=0.069 (but still not explicitly PRS-only). PGS002038 and PGS001831 come from a portability framework paper and lack AUROC/R², but provide PRS-comparable partial-r (0.0396 and 0.0367) and use genome-wide shrinkage/penalized regression methods; they are ranked ahead of PGS004699 because PGS004699’s context is prediction at optic neuritis presentation (potentially a more packaged/clinical setting) and its reported AUROC is full-model only despite very large validation size, which is a weak differentiator.

Direct-match candidates for myocardial infarction are present (multiple models with trait_efo/phenotyping_reported explicitly myocardial infarction, including PheCode 411.2 MI, UKB MI/acute MI, and ICD10 I21 acute MI). The best-supported choice from the visible evidence is PGS005039 because it is an explicit MI endpoint (PheCode 411.2; phenotyping_reported: Myocardial infarction), comes from a disease-focused MI comparison paper (not a pan-trait sparse framework), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (ldpred) with very large variant count (~1.29M), and shows the strongest reported discrimination among the MI PheCode set (C-index ~0.7848) with a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.578, 95% CI 1.50–1.67). Key limitation: across the top MI PheCode models (PGS005035/038/039/044/045 etc.) the reported C-index values are extremely close and all are evaluated on European ancestry (selected_validation_ancestry: European), so the ranking is sensitive to small, likely-noisy metric differences and lacks clear multi-ancestry external-validation separation; additionally, several other direct-match MI models exist (e.g., UKB snpnet MI family; ICD10 I21 acute MI) but are either from a pan-trait sparse framework or have less comparable/less complete PRS-only evidence in the visible fields, leaving some residual uncertainty.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are J33 Nasal polyp / Nasal Cavity Polyp) and come from the same publication, with identical training cohort (UKB), training size (n=174,489), validation size (n=56,192), ancestry (DEV/EVAL EUR), and variant count (1,059,939), so endpoint fidelity and transportability context do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, leaving effect size as the main differentiator; PGS004535 reports a stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.600668) than PGS004465 (OR=1.3496), which is supportive of better discriminative signal. However, covariates are listed as Unknown for both and the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 limits certainty, so the direct-match recommendation is not high-confidence.

Both visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (trait_efo = nicotine dependence; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Tobacco use disorder) and come from the same UKB portability publication with similar basic covariates and identical training/validation sample sizes, so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiator in the visible evidence is comparable performance: PGS002037 reports a higher selected European partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741, CI 0.0601–0.0881) than PGS001830 (0.0557, CI 0.0416–0.0697), and it uses an LDpred2 genome-wide shrinkage approach with substantially more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is a supportive structural signal when endpoints are otherwise aligned. Confidence is Moderate because both models are near-clones from the same framework-style portability study and neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect sizes in the visible metadata, limiting the strength of the performance comparison beyond partial-r.

Direct-match candidates are present for nodular goiter via (i) benign nodular goiter models (PGS005261/PGS005262/PGS005263) and (ii) closely related multinodular/nontoxic goiter models (PGS001814/PGS002022). PGS005262 is best supported because it has the closest phenotype alignment to the target (“Benign nodular goiter” with matching EFO) and, among the benign nodular goiter siblings, it shows the strongest reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.5933) while using a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRSCS) with very large variant count (~1.09M), a positive structural signal. Runners-up are ranked by remaining direct-match support: PGS005273 and PGS005274 are still direct-match (case-control contrast includes benign nodular goiter explicitly) and have higher AUROC (~0.617/0.613) but are less endpoint-faithful to ‘nodular goiter’ because they target “thyroid carcinoma vs benign nodular goiter” rather than goiter status itself; PGS005263 is the next-best benign-goiter sibling (PRSCS, ~1.09M variants, AUROC 0.5876); PGS005261 is the weakest benign-goiter sibling (P+T, 110 variants, AUROC 0.5854). Overall outcome is DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL because key comparability evidence is limited: the 2026 medRxiv family reports only full-model AUROC with covariates listed as Unknown (so PRS-only performance and covariate inflation cannot be assessed), while the UKB portability models (PGS001814/PGS002022) provide PRS-comparable partial-r but are from a portability framework and show small effects (partial-r ~0.024–0.028), leaving some unresolved uncertainty in cross-study metric comparability and true standalone PRS strength.

All 10 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (obesity) via trait_efo and/or phenotyping_reported. PGS005235 is best supported because its endpoint fidelity is strong (phenotyping_reported: obesity phecode 278.1), it uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) appropriate for a highly polygenic trait, it has broad multi-cohort GWAS/training provenance listed (EGG, GIANT, UKB), and it reports a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.97), which domain guidance treats as meaningful discrimination evidence when PRS-only AUC/R² are absent. Runners-up: PGS004447 is also an obesity ICD10 (E66) score with a strong genome-wide method (LDpred2) and large variant count, but has weaker effect-size evidence (OR≈1.36) and unknown covariates; PGS005154 and PGS005145 are endpoint-faithful obesity scores evaluated in East Asian cohorts with genome-wide methods and large variant counts, but their non-EUR-only evaluation makes them less generally supported absent a specified deployment ancestry; PGS002033 is a portability-framework score ("Portability of 245 polygenic scores") with LDpred2 and a stronger partial-r than its penalized-regression sibling, but framework provenance is a negative signal versus more disease-focused candidates. Overall confidence is limited because most candidates lack PRS-comparable AUC/R², several have unknown covariates, and the pool mixes different endpoint constructions (phecode/ICD10 vs time-to-event vs broad overweight/overnutrition composites), leaving some unresolved comparability.

All 13 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (osteoporosis) by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported, but the pool is dominated by framework/portability-style scores and several newer models lack PRS-comparable metrics (AUC/R2) and/or have unknown covariates, limiting a clearly high-quality pick.

PGS001274 is preferred because it has strong endpoint alignment to osteoporosis (phenotyping_reported: time-to-event osteoporosis without pathological fracture; still mapped to osteoporosis), reports explicit PRS-only performance metrics (PGS AUROC (no covariates)=0.57595; PGS R2 (no covariates)=0.00945) plus incremental AUROC (0.00777) with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), and has a reasonably large validation sample (n=24,905). Among the candidates with PRS-only metrics, it also has slightly stronger PRS-only AUROC/R2 than its closest sibling.

Runners-up: (1) PGS001273 is the closest sibling with the same framework origin and similar endpoint but slightly weaker PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.5685; PGS R2 0.00688). (2) PGS004565 and (3) PGS004560 are endpoint-faithful (osteoporosis / M81 osteoporosis without pathological fracture) and show moderate per-SD ORs (~1.33 and ~1.32), but lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and list covariates as Unknown, reducing comparability. (4) PGS002768 is endpoint-faithful and reports OR=1.31 (moderate), but provides no PRS-comparable metrics and has limited visible training details (samples_training N/A; no training cohorts listed).

Main limitation: the best-supported metric-bearing options (PGS001274/PGS001273) come from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (a known weaker archetype per the provided domain knowledge), while several potentially stronger modern genome-wide/ensemble scores lack comparable PRS-only metrics and/or have unknown covariates—so the selection is evidence-limited rather than decisively best-in-class.

Two direct-match candidates are present (both map to trait_efo=otosclerosis). PGS002046 is preferred because its phenotyping_reported is a straightforward disease endpoint (“Otosclerosis”) rather than time-to-event (“TTE otosclerosis”) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with substantially more variants (570,308), which is a positive structural signal for polygenic traits. However, the evidence is limited because PGS002046 lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R² in the provided metrics (only partial-r is reported), making it hard to compare directly against PGS001255, which does report PGS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC. PGS001255 is additionally penalized by being from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework paper (“across 813 traits”) and by its time-to-event endpoint, but it has more explicit discrimination reporting. With only two candidates and mixed strengths (endpoint/method vs metric availability), the direct-match selection is sub-optimal and confidence is low. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

Direct-match candidates are present, including multiple models explicitly mapped to the target EFO term (ovarian neoplasm) with phenotyping_reported = "Malignant neoplasm of ovary" (PGS000544–PGS000564 etc.). Among these exact-endpoint candidates, PGS000549 has the strongest visible comparable performance signal in its selected validation record (highest full-model AUROC among the ovarian-neoplasm-labeled set shown: 0.567 with EUR evaluation) and also the strongest per-SD effect size (OR 1.263, 95% CI 1.15–1.387) plus the highest reported pseudo-R² (0.00996) in that same family, making it the best-supported direct match from the visible list. Runners-up are chosen from the same exact-endpoint family with very similar design/ancestry but slightly weaker AUROC/R²/effect-size evidence: PGS000550 (AUROC 0.568; pseudo-R² 0.0113; OR 1.286), PGS000551 (AUROC 0.558; pseudo-R² 0.00819; OR 1.234), PGS000560 (AUROC 0.552; pseudo-R² 0.00819; OR 1.233), and PGS000564 (AUROC 0.556; pseudo-R² 0.00692; OR 1.215). Confidence is Moderate because (i) these are all from the same PRSweb framework publication with broadly similar metadata and only full-model AUROC (no explicit PRS-only AUROC/R²), and (ii) several non-neoplasm-labeled but closely aligned ovarian-cancer models in the list show higher full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS003385) yet differ in endpoint/subtype, so the exact-target ranking relies on limited comparable metrics within the exact-label cluster. | Borda re-rank promoted runner-up to primary.

All 11 visible candidates are direct matches to the target trait (pancreatic carcinoma) via pancreatic cancer / exocrine pancreatic carcinoma / pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma endpoints. PGS000083 is best supported overall because it has strong endpoint fidelity (incident pancreatic cancer), large European validation (n=391,491), and supportive effect-size evidence (HR=1.49, 95% CI 1.36–1.62) alongside reported discrimination (AUROC=0.745; C-index=0.742) in the selected European validation record. However, confidence is not High because the reported AUROC/C-index are full-model metrics with a relatively heavy covariate set (including family history, BMI, and smoking variables), and no PRS-only AUROC/R2 is provided, limiting comparability across candidates. Runners-up: PGS000794 is essentially the same 22-variant score family with similar full-model metrics but uses inverse weights (making it less straightforward as a primary choice despite similar support); PGS000725 and PGS000663 are similar 22-variant genome-wide-significant scores with large/cleaner-looking evaluation contexts but lower reported full-model AUROC (0.639 and 0.67, respectively) and/or smaller validation (PGS000663 n=956); PGS002264 targets the clinically dominant subtype (pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma) and reports high AUROC (0.83) but appears to be a risk-prediction package integrating diabetes mellitus and other clinical risk covariates, making the full-model AUROC less informative for standalone PRS quality.

All 11 listed candidates are direct matches at the disease-concept level (trait_efo=Parkinson disease), but several have endpoint shifts (progression/cognitive decline/dementia/incident-only) or covariate-heavy full-model reporting that limits clean PRS-only comparability. PGS000903 is best supported because it targets Parkinson’s disease status (phenotyping_reported: Parkinson’s disease), comes from a large disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis publication family (Lancet Neurol 2021), uses a more polygenic construction than GWAS-hits-only siblings (C+T with 1,805 variants), and provides the strongest directly PRS-relevant effect evidence in the visible set (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25 with CI) plus an R² value (0.054), whereas most others lack PRS-comparable metrics. Remaining limitation: the reported AUROC (0.692) appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only) and covariates are included (PCs, age, sex), so cross-model metric comparability is imperfect; additionally, some alternatives report higher full-model AUROC but with heavier non-genetic covariates (e.g., family history), which is discounted. Runners-up: PGS000902 is the closest sibling from the same strong publication family with the same endpoint but is GWAS-hits-only (90 variants) and has lower reported AUROC; PGS003763 has a very large incident-PD evaluation and a strong HR (1.72) but is incident-only; PGS000123 is a clean PD-status endpoint with effect evidence but lacks comparable discrimination metrics; PGS001774 reports high AUROC (0.8) but uses many non-genetic risk-factor covariates (including family history), making the metric less informative for standalone PRS ranking.

All 4 candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target concept (peripheral vascular disease), but they differ in endpoint fidelity and evidence strength. PGS005217 is best supported because it targets a closely aligned clinical endpoint (incident peripheral artery disease), is disease-focused (JAMA Cardiol PAD study with many contributing cohorts), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with very large variant count (1,296,292), and reports a strong per-SD effect size (HR=1.66, 95% CI 1.61–1.71) plus a C-index/full-model metric (0.731) with relatively basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Main limitation: the target is broader (PVD) than PAD and the reported discrimination is not explicitly PRS-only (full-model C-index), so comparability is imperfect.

Runners-up: PGS002055 and PGS001843 are exact-label matches to ‘peripheral vascular disease, unspecified’ (trait_efo matches), but they come from a UKB portability framework paper and only report small partial correlations (0.0175 and 0.0151, respectively), which is weak PRS signal and framework-origin is a negative per the provided domain guidance; between them, PGS002055 is preferred due to higher partial-r and a stronger genome-wide method/structure (LDpred2 with 599,514 variants vs penalized regression with 242 variants). PGS005158 is PAD-focused but restricted to type 2 diabetes (phenotyping_reported) with very heavy clinical covariate adjustment and only a modest HR (1.13), making it less suitable for generic PVD; it is therefore ranked last.

Direct-match candidates are present (all have trait_efo = preeclampsia), but the pool is small and none reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so selection relies mainly on endpoint fidelity and effect-size evidence.
